items.title: Tech stocks today: SpaceX, AMD top quarterly results, but fail to impress Wall Street. Shares sink
items.summary: Tech stocks coverage for the week of Aug. 3.

items.title: AI CapEx fears: Is big tech overspending?
items.summary: Host Kenny Polcari joins Man Group Chief Market Strategist Kristina Hooper and Legato Financial CIO Ryan Kelly to debate the risks of massive AI CapEx spending and how a hawkish Federal Reserve could impact markets ahead of the midterms.

items.title: Who Might Buy Snap If Its Founders Ever Decide to Sell
items.summary: Snap's stock has cratered while nearly a billion users keep scrolling, and that gap between price and audience has a handful of tech giants quietly doing the math. The catch is a pair of founders who may have no intention of answering the phone.

items.title: Mark Zuckerberg Wrote That AI May Soon Deliver "Personal Superintelligence to Everyone" Just Before Meta's Free Cash Flow Cratered 91%. Do Investors Buy the Vision?
items.summary: Superintelligence is a form of artificial intelligence that can surpass the cognitive abilities of humans.

items.title: Mark Zuckerberg's Meta Just Suffered an 11-Day Losing Streak That Erased $17.8 Billion From His Net Worth. Is the AI Bet Still Worth It?
items.summary: Investors are increasingly concerned about Meta's AI spending and its impact on the company's cash flow.

items.title: Landowners Near Meta’s New Data Center Struck Gold. Retirees Renting on Social Security Could Be Priced Out.
items.summary: When Meta announced a $50 billion data center in a Louisiana parish of 20,000 people, some landowners became overnight millionaires. For retirees living on Social Security and a monthly lease, the same project set off a very different kind of countdown.

items.title: New report warns China transceiver ban would hurt U.S. AI giants
items.summary: Investing.com - Chinese optical module makers control roughly two-thirds of global transceiver supply, and no Western alternative can absorb that volume within the next one to two years, Counterpoint Research warned — a finding that casts doubt on whether a proposed U.S. import ban can be executed without damaging the AI infrastructure buildout it is meant to protect.
